name: Githeri
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 2 cups dried maize kernels or fresh maize
2 cups dried beans (kidney beans, red beans, or mixed beans)

steps: Wash the maize and beans thoroughly. If using dried maize and beans, soak them overnight in separate bowls of water.
Drain the soaked maize and beans and place them in a large pot.
Add enough water to cover the mixture and boil until both the maize and beans become soft. This may take 1–2 hours depending on the type used.
In another pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and cook until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, carrot, and bell pepper. Cook for several minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add curry powder or turmeric if desired.
Add the cooked maize and beans to the vegetable mixture and stir well.
Season with salt and simmer for 10–15 minutes, adding a little water if necessary.

culture.text: Githeri (Gĩtheri), also called muthere or mutheri, mûthekia-ngûkû is a traditional Kenyan meal consisting of maize kernels and legumes mixed and boiled together. The maize and beans are mixed in a sufuria, a type of pot, with water added, and the mixture is boiled until fully cooked.
